Its small-theta coefficient (1-b²)(1-5b²)/24 is negative for a>5/2, but exponential tail is positive, giving at least one positive root. Along every positive root as a→∞, bounded u forces theta bounded and leads to theta tanh theta=theta² (impossible except zero), while the uniform negative small-theta coefficient also excludes theta→0. Thus u→∞, tanh(b theta)→1 superexponentially, and u-2log u=log a+O(1/a). On the increasing branch, u=H+2log H+4log H/H+O((log H)^2/H²); converting theta/a=u/(a eps) changes only O(H/a). Independent high precision exact root checks over six finite c values corroborated the asymptotic but finite scans do not prove all-root assertion.
